correctness.rationale: For positive connected transmission and nonzero initial seeding, N_j(t) is bounded below by Z_j>0 from N_j=N_j0-mu_j integral I and R_j=R_j0+gamma_j integral I; integrated log S and log N give the exact final-size formula. F_i(y)=sum_j a_ij log[N_j/(Z_j+epsilon_j S_j0 e^-y_j)] maps the nonnegative orthant into [c,M] with c>0 and has positive first and negative second coordinate derivatives. Concavity plus positive offset proves uniqueness via maximal coordinate ratio; a tangent argument gives u_n-y* <=(K-1)q^n y* and l_n >=(1-q^n)y*, hence width <=Kq^nM, with no contraction restriction. Symbolic differentiation, exact off-H2 inequalities and high-precision/rational probes in checker.py passed. No numerical probes are used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact motivating preprint and open-access journal article state an unresolved all-parameter uniqueness question outside four regimes, while guaranteeing a usable rate only in a contraction regime. The present model-specific positivity/concavity conjugacy closes that question, extends to arbitrary finite-group mixing, and supplies an explicit and computable parameter-only stopping certificate for final susceptible counts. A biologically admissible rational example violates all four older conditions, confirming a genuinely additional parameter regime. Generic antecedent theorems are fully credited; scientific value is the missing model-specific classification and interval computation.
